_readme: Curated NASA archival records and attributed findings. Gameplay coefficients are defined separately in story-plan.md and src/game/scenes.js.

events.dataset: NASA DONKI (Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information)
events.speed_note: Two analyses are marked most accurate: 2678 km/s for the shock feature and 1927 km/s for the bulk leading edge. These are distinct analyses, not a measured Mars dose or a statistical uncertainty interval.
events.sourceNote: The DONKI note describes a fast halo CME with a believed backsided source. A concurrent C6.7 flare is explicitly excluded as its source in that note.

alert.summary: The linked alert and model outputs list predictions for spacecraft including Juno and Solar Orbiter; Mars is not an identified impact target in this record.

events.direction_note: The existing [176, 0] longitude/latitude pair refers to the bulk analysis. The shock analysis has [172, 2]; see analyses_most_accurate.
events.flareCatalogueNote: No inference about missing FLR/SEP catalogue entries is required or established by this source audit.

findings.title: NASA Watches Mars Light Up During Epic Solar Storm
facts: NASA reports a major May 20, 2024 solar event affecting Mars; its estimated X12 flare classification used Solar Orbiter data.
The article reports 8100 micrograys for a hypothetical astronaut beside Curiosity, describing it as equivalent to about 30 chest X-rays and not deadly in that reported case.
The article describes the largest surge measured by Curiosity RAD during its first 12 years on Mars.
MAVEN observations documented a strong solar energetic particle event and ultraviolet auroras.
The article explains that terrain can provide additional shielding; this game does not calculate human exposure or medical outcomes.

linkNote: The DONKI record and NASA Mars article refer to the same date, but an event-level match has not been established. Present them as independently cited archival examples. DONKI is not a Mars surface-dose measurement.
usageInGame: Active Scene 5 science card: independent examples of a near-Sun CME record and a Mars radiation observation. Safety effects are fictional. Detailed attribution must remain visible in the interface.
